correctness.rationale: For a finite poset, an antichain S is shattered by ideals of size k iff |down(S)|<=k<=|P|-|up(S)|; the interval of ideals supports every intermediate cardinality. In an m-by-(2m-2) grid, an (m-1)-cell antichain omits one row; at most m-1 cells in that row are incomparable to S. The shattering inequalities force equality and therefore every unused column belongs to one gap in that row, uniquely determining S_h and area k_h=m(m+1)/2-1+(h-1)(m-2). An m-cell antichain has no incomparable cells and cannot be shattered. This proves all-rank necessity/sufficiency, including boundaries. The standalone checker independently tests 19,307 direct trace instances at m=3,4,5 and 39,441 closure computations at m=6,7,8. Finite tests are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Prescribed-area rank sections of the classical distributive lattice of Young diagrams are a natural, studied hypothesis family. Although their numbers vary unimodally with area, maximal Boolean cell shattering is sharply nonmonotone: exactly m regularly separated ranks each have a unique top-dimensional face, and the intervening ranks have none. This is an all-parameter structural facet-rigidity theorem, with concrete extremal examples, not a routine numeric census or generic restatement of the trace test.
